title: KVCache host swap schedulers and thresholds
content:
Purpose and scope

This note proposes a practical host-swap + paging scheduling strategy for the KV cache used by the serving runtime. It focuses on multi-tier residency decisions (device HBM -> device-host-pinned -> host DRAM (local/remote) -> NVMe), explicit PCIe/UMA-aware thresholds, and a scheduler that balances tail latency for latency-sensitive requests against throughput/cost for bulk workloads.

Goals
- Keep 99th percentile latency regressions minimal for latency-sensitive endpoints while using host memory to increase effective cache capacity.
- Avoid saturating PCIe (or interconnects for UMA remote memory) and host swap causing long stalls.
- Provide simple tunable thresholds + adaptive hysteresis so ops can roll out progressively.
- Produce telemetry that makes it easy to correlate evictions/prefetches with backend latencies and PCIe counters.

Key constraints and observations
- PCIe latency penalty for a large KV chunk (typical 64KB entry or a 2MB hugepage-backed slab) is dominated by transfer and small queue delays: empirically 200–800us depending on link/saturation.
- NUMA/UMA remote memory access cost can be 2–10x local DRAM latency and should be treated separately from PCIe device host transfers.
- Small frequent migrations (many tiny entries) amplify overhead due to per-request PCIe setup and copy overhead; batching helps.
- Large concurrent prefetch/evict jobs can overwhelm the PCIe fabric; we must limit concurrency and use a feedback loop based on measured PCIe bandwidth and tail latency signals.

Design overview
1) Residency tiers and cataloging - Device local HBM (resident) — fastest, smallest quota.
- Device-host pinned pages (dma-buffer) — used for warmed pages that are expected to be reused soon and avoid remapping cost.
- Host DRAM (local NUMA node) — fast but with PCIe transfer latency to GPU.
- Host DRAM (remote NUMA / UMA) — higher access cost; consider as last in DRAM tier.
- NVMe swap — fallback for cold entries, used when host memory pressure is high or for long-term overflow.

2) Decision primitives (signals)
- recency_score: decay-based score from last access timestamp.
- reuse_freq: historical hits per time-window (e.g., 5m).
- entry_size_bytes: bucketized to avoid oscillation with tiny vs huge entries.
- reload_cost_est: estimate of PCIe transfer time + kernel copy overhead for the entry.
- pcie_bandwidth_util: 1m and 10s moving averages from hw counters.
- host_mem_headroom: free host DRAM on relevant NUMA node.
- gpu_cache_occupancy: fraction of configured device KV quota used.
- request_class: latency-sensitive | best-effort | background (derived from route/model metadata).

3) Eviction scoring and policy
Score(entry) = alpha * recency_score + beta * log(1 + reuse_freq) - gamma * (1 / reload_cost_est) - delta * size_penalty

Where coefficients are tuned per request_class. For latency-sensitive: higher weight on recency and reload_cost (i.e., prefer to keep entries that are cheap to reload and have high recency). For throughput routes: more aggressive eviction of cold entries.

Numeric starting defaults (empirical; to be tuned in experiments)
- device_quota_fill_trigger = 0.78 (start evicting when occupancy > 78%)
- aggressive_eviction_trigger = 0.92 (forced compaction when > 92%)
- pcie_bandwidth_soft_limit = 0.65 (if avg PCIe util > 65%, throttle prefetch/restore ops)
- pcie_bandwidth_hard_limit = 0.85 (stop background migration until drops below 70%)
- prefetch_reuse_prob_threshold = 0.6 (only prefetch entries with predicted reuse probability > 60%)
- host_headroom_safe_bytes = 1.0 * model_working_set (keep at least 1x model working set free on host before NVMe use)
- batch_eviction_target = 64 entries (or ~4MB), max_batch_ms = 20ms per eviction worker
- background_worker_limit = min(4, cpu_count/4)

4) PCIe/UMA-aware feedback controller
- Use a simple PID-like controller that adjusts per-node prefetch concurrency and small-batch sizes based on pcie_bandwidth_util and observed GPU tail latency. If pcie_bandwidth_util rises above soft_limit, reduce concurrency and increase batching to amortize. If above hard_limit, pause non-critical migrations and force smaller active device working set.
- Track pct of requests that suffered a device cache miss that required synchronous page transfers; this is the primary signal to avoid thrash.

5) Prefetch and restoration rules
- Synchronous restore (on miss): For latency-sensitive requests, if reload_cost_est < latency_budget_margin (e.g., 2x mean rpc latency budget), do synchronous restore. Otherwise fallback to smaller model variant or steer to best-effort path.
- Asynchronous prefetch: For requests predicted to access a set (from prompt signature or trace-based fingerprints), schedule prefetch if predicted combined reload_cost < prefetch_budget and pcie util < soft_limit.

6) Host-side mechanisms and kernel integration
- Prefer using userfaultfd for zero-copy on-demand page population where supported; fall back to explicit dma transfers + memcpy.
- Use madvise(MADV_DONTFORK | MADV_WILLNEED) hints for prefetch jobs.
- Allocate larger slab pages (2MB hugepages) for large entries to reduce descriptor churn; bucketize small entries to pack into 64KB sub-slabs to reduce PCIe per-entry overhead.

7) Hysteresis and safety
- All thresholds use hysteresis windows (e.g., require metric to be above threshold for 3 consecutive samples over 1s buckets before triggering heavy actions).
- Conservative rollback: if tail latency jumps by > 15% after a parameter change, automatically revert prefetch aggressiveness by one step and emit alert.

8) Telemetry and dashboards (must ship with policy)
Metric names to produce:
- kvcache.device.occupancy.pct (per-GPU)
- kvcache.host.transfer.bytes/sec (per-node)
- kvcache.migrations.inflight.count
- kvcache.reload.latency.p50/p95/p99
- kvcache.evictions.count.by_reason (memory_pressure, pcie_throttle, policy)
- kvcache.prefetch.hits_vs_total

Dashboards: correlation view of pcie bandwidth util vs reload p99 vs model endpoint p99; an alert rule that fires when reload p99 exceeds 2ms *AND* pcie_util > 0.7.

9) Experiments and validation plan
Stage A (simulation): run randomized synthetic replay of request traces to validate scoring function and estimate baseline tail. Stage B (canary on dev cluster): enable host-swap with conservative defaults on non-customer models for 24–48 hrs. Stage C (staged rollout): ramp to 10%, 30%, 60% in production, monitoring tail latency and PCIe util.

Experiment metrics: per-route tail latency delta, transfer bytes/sec, migrations/sec, synchronous-restores/sec, host memory used for KV, NVMe swap bytes.

10) Rollout knobs and ops playbook
- knob: device_quota_fill_trigger (float)
- knob: pcie_bandwidth_soft_limit & hard_limit (float)
- knob: background_worker_limit (int)
- knob: prefetch_reuse_prob_threshold (float)

Ops playbook snippets:
- If p99 rises and pcie_util > 0.7: reduce background_worker_limit by half and set prefetch_reuse_prob_threshold -> 0.8.
- If host mem < host_headroom_safe_bytes: pause prefetch and start NVMe eviction to create headroom.

Open questions and future work
- Better per-entry reload cost modeling that accounts for PCIe topology (x16 vs x8 lanes, multi-root complex sharing) and concurrent kernel copy overhead.
- Explore RDMA-like direct access to host pages from accelerator for UMA setups to avoid explicit DMA copies.
- Auto-tune coefficients (alpha/beta/gamma) with continuous shadow experiments per-route.

Appendix: sample eviction pseudocode (simplified)
for each eviction_cycle:
  gather candidate_entries from LRU window and high_reuse_histogram
  for e in candidate_entries:
    compute score(e) = alpha*recency(e) + beta*log(1+freq(e)) - gamma*(1/reload_cost(e)) - delta*size_bucket_penalty(e)
  sort candidates ascending (lowest score first)
  batch = take up to batch_eviction_target where pcie_util < soft_limit and host_headroom sufficient
  schedule dma_transfer(batch) with priority class = background unless route is latency-sensitive

Note: keep the implementation small and incremental. Start with a single-node feedback controller and only a couple of thresholds to make troubleshooting straightforward.
